name: Thermostat Adapter

steps.text: Make sure a compatible Totaline/Venstar thermostat is installed.
Plug the Thermostat Adapter into the jack on the bottom of the thermostat.
steps.expect: Status LED turns on solid green

notes: Compatible with Totaline/Venstar T1700, T1800 and T1900 thermostats (Venstar 30410A, 30411A and 30412A); the location's wiring should have 5 wires.
Powered by the thermostat; no batteries needed.
As an RF-only device it needs at least one dual-band device such as an Access Point 2443; at least two are recommended.

steps.text: Set the thermostat to the mode, setpoint and fan setting you want.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Status LED blinks; thermostat display flashes all characters once

notes: As controller (reporting A/C, heat or fan on and off): set the thermostat to A/C, Heat or FanOn (for FanOn also set the thermostat to Off mode), do these steps, then press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds. The status LED stops blinking and the display flashes once.

As responder: set the thermostat to the state to recall, put the controller in linking mode, then tap the SET button once (for the controller's on command) or twice (for its off command) and press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds. The display flashes all characters twice. Link the on and off buttons separately.

To enable change reports to home automation software, set the thermostat to Off mode, press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds, then press and hold the interface's SET button for 3 seconds. Reports go only to the last device linked this way.

verification.note: The Thermostat Adapter 2441V Owner's Manual says to hold the SET button for 3 seconds and gives no timeout for the Thermostat Adapter's own linking mode; the Thermostat Adapter 2441V Quick Start Guide says to hold it for about 5 seconds and that linking mode times out after 4 minutes. The catalog uses the owner's manual's 3 seconds and the quick start guide's 4 minutes.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Set the thermostat to Off mode, so the link also enables change reports to the Hub.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Status LED blinks; thermostat display flashes all characters once

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: Change reports go only to the last device linked with the thermostat in Off mode.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the Insteon Developer's Guide (2009)'s Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping commands; no document describes adding this product to a Hub. The Off mode step for change reports is read from this profile's linking notes.

The Insteon Developer's Guide (2009) says i1 devices don't support Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), and the catalog doesn't know the engine of every version of this product. An i2 or i2CS version takes it; ask the device with Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) first.
Read from the From a Hub alternative to this profile's linking, whose steps are assembled from its own linking steps and standard Insteon commands; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Status LED blinks; thermostat display flashes all characters once

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds again.
steps.expect: Status LED keeps blinking; display flashes all characters once

notes: Then press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds; the status LED stops blinking and the display flashes once.

To unlink the Thermostat Adapter from a controller, put the controller in unlinking mode, tap the Thermostat Adapter's SET button, then press and hold it for 3 seconds (display flashes twice). This erases all commands linked to that controller, even those on other buttons; re-link the ones you want to keep.
With the thermostat in Off mode, the same unlinking steps followed by the interface's SET button disable change reports.

verification.note: The steps are from the Thermostat Adapter 2441V Owner's Manual, which gives a 4-minute timeout only for the controller's linking and unlinking modes when the Thermostat Adapter is the responder. No document gives a timeout for the Thermostat Adapter's own unlinking mode; the Thermostat Adapter 2441V Quick Start Guide gives 4 minutes for its linking mode.

steps.text: Unlink the Thermostat Adapter from its controllers and unlink its responders.
Open the thermostat cover and, while pressing the small round button on the bottom center of the thermostat, gently pull the Thermostat Adapter down.
Wait 10 seconds.
While pressing and holding the SET button, plug the Thermostat Adapter back into the thermostat.
Keep holding the SET button for 3 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: Status LED stays off about 20 seconds, the display flashes all characters three times, then the LED flickers and turns on solid

notes: Clears all Insteon links, setpoints and other settings.

steps.text: Unlink the Thermostat Adapter from every controller it is linked to.
Open the front cover of the thermostat by gently pulling its right edge toward you.
While pressing firmly on the small round button on the bottom center of the thermostat, gently pull the Thermostat Adapter down.

notes: If it isn't unlinked, controllers keep retrying commands and slow the system.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove every link between the Hub and the device with no SET button press. First the device's group 1 link: Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) is sent to the device while the modem joins as responder. Then the modem's group 0 link: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09). This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

Inferred: seen on an i2CS device (I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245: unlinking by the modem's own records left the device's records for the Hub's other groups, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. So a device that still answers the Hub after removal may hold other records for it; a factory reset, as the Thermostat Adapter 2441V Owner's Manual gives it, clears them. This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

verification.note: Assembled from the Insteon Developer's Guide (2009)'s Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode commands; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: It links to group 1 while cooling, group 2 while heating and group 3 while its fan runs; devices linked to group 239 (0xEF) get its status reports.
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)
